subject: english
text: Mia stood at the edge of the cold pool, reluctant to jump. Her toes curled over the tiles while her friends splashed and called her name.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "reluctant" mean?
parts.explanation: Mia hesitated and did not want to jump, so "reluctant" means unwilling.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "reluctant" correctly?

options.text: I keep my reluctant in a box under the bed.
Dad was reluctant to lend his new bike, so he asked us to be careful.
She reluctant walked to school every morning.
The soup was so reluctant that it burned my tongue.

parts.explanation: Being reluctant means not wanting to do something, so Dad asking us to be careful fits. The other sentences use the word for the opposite meaning or in the wrong form.

hints: Look at what Mia's toes and friends are doing.

subject: english
text: Grandma wrapped the fragile teacup in three layers of soft cloth. Even a small bump in the suitcase could have shattered it.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "fragile" mean?
parts.explanation: A cup that a small bump could shatter is easily broken, which is what fragile means.

parts.prompt: The glass sculpture was so ____ that the museum kept it in a locked case.
parts.explanation: A glass sculpture that needs a locked case breaks easily, so fragile fits. Sturdy means strong, which does not match.

hints: What could happen to the cup in a bumpy suitcase?

subject: english
text: After the spring rain, wildflowers were abundant on the hillside. There were so many that the whole slope looked yellow.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "abundant" mean?
parts.explanation: The whole slope looked yellow because there were so many flowers, so abundant means plentiful.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "abundant" correctly?

options.text: The desert had an abundant of sand.
Only one abundant apple was left in the bowl.
Water is abundant in the rainforest, so the animals never go thirsty.
She felt abundant when she lost her favourite toy.

parts.explanation: Abundant means plentiful, and a rainforest with lots of water fits. The others use it to mean sad, a single item, or the wrong part of speech.

hints: Think about the whole slope looking yellow.

subject: english
text: The old clock made a peculiar noise, somewhere between a hiccup and a whistle. Nobody in the family had ever heard anything like it.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "peculiar" mean?
parts.explanation: Nobody had heard such a noise before, which tells us peculiar means strange.

parts.prompt: Jack noticed a ____ smell coming from the cupboard, unlike anything he knew.
parts.explanation: A smell unlike anything he knew is unusual, so peculiar fits. Ordinary means normal, which is the opposite.

hints: Notice how the sound is described: not like anything heard before.

subject: english
text: Leo was cautious as he crossed the wobbly log over the creek. He tested each step before putting his weight down.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "cautious" mean?
parts.explanation: Leo tested every step to stay safe, so cautious means careful.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "cautious" correctly?

options.text: The cautious puppy ran wildly through the puddles without looking.
She was cautious to win the race by a mile.
A cautious driver slows down when the road is wet.

parts.explanation: Cautious means careful about danger, so slowing down on a wet road fits. The other sentences give it the wrong meaning or the wrong form.

hints: What does Leo do before each step?

subject: english
text: An enormous whale rose beside the small boat. The children gasped, because it was longer than their school bus.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "enormous" mean?
parts.explanation: The whale was longer than a school bus, so enormous means extremely large.

parts.prompt: The elephant was so ____ that it filled the whole doorway of the barn.
parts.explanation: Filling a whole doorway means being huge, so enormous fits. Tiny is the opposite.

hints: Compare the whale to the school bus.

subject: english
text: If you hesitate at the top of the slide, the queue behind you will grow. Take a breath and go when you are ready.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "hesitate" mean?

options.text: to pause because you are unsure

parts.explanation: Pausing at the top while unsure is what hesitate means.

parts.prompt: Please do not ____ to ask me if you need any help with your homework.
parts.explanation: The sentence tells you not to pause or feel unsure about asking, so hesitate fits. The other words do not make sense here.

hints: What is the person standing at the top of the slide doing?

subject: english
text: The antique dealer checked the coin carefully and smiled. It was a genuine gold coin, not a clever copy.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "genuine" mean?
parts.explanation: It was a real coin and not a copy, so genuine means real.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "genuine" correctly?

options.text: The genuine mountain was very tall and cold.
He genuine apologised to his teacher.
Her smile was genuine because she was truly happy to see us.
The genuine painting was painted by a machine to look like a copy.

parts.explanation: Genuine means real and sincere, so a smile that comes from true happiness fits. The others do not use the word correctly.

hints: The dealer contrasts it with a copy.

subject: english
text: Mr Singh was generous with his time and his garden. Every summer he shared his tomatoes with all the neighbours.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "generous" mean?

options.text: willing to give or share freely

parts.explanation: He shared his tomatoes with everyone, so generous means happy to give.

parts.prompt: The ____ girl gave half of her lunch to a classmate who had forgotten his.
parts.explanation: Giving away half her lunch is sharing freely, so generous fits.

hints: What does Mr Singh do with his tomatoes?

subject: english
text: Deep in the desert, explorers found the ruins of an ancient city. Its stone walls had stood for more than three thousand years.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "ancient" mean?
parts.explanation: Walls standing for three thousand years tells us ancient means very old.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "ancient" correctly?

options.text: My ancient sister was born last week.
The ancient puppy chased its tail all day because it was so young.
We bought an ancient phone this morning from the shop's new range.
The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids thousands of years ago.

parts.explanation: Ancient means from a very long time ago, so the pyramids fit. The other sentences describe new or young things.

hints: How many years had the walls stood?

subject: english
text: The bridge was closed, so the council built a temporary path across the creek. It would only be used until the repairs were finished.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "temporary" mean?
parts.explanation: The path was only used until repairs finished, so temporary means short-lived.

parts.prompt: Our school is using a ____ classroom while the new building is finished.
parts.explanation: A classroom used only until the new building is ready lasts a short time, so temporary fits. Permanent means lasting forever.

hints: Read the last sentence: until when would the path be used?

subject: english
text: The netball team was victorious after a tense final match. They hugged each other and held the shining trophy high.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "victorious" mean?
parts.explanation: They won the final and held the trophy, so victorious means having won.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "victorious" correctly?

options.text: He was victorious when he lost every game.
The victorious soup was hot and tasty.
The victorious runner crossed the finish line first and raised her arms.

parts.explanation: Victorious means having won, so a runner finishing first fits. The others contradict it or use the wrong form.

hints: What are they holding up at the end?

subject: english
text: The map was accurate down to the smallest creek. Using it, the scouts found the hidden campsite without a single wrong turn.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "accurate" mean?
parts.explanation: The map led them without a wrong turn because it was exact, so accurate means correct.

parts.prompt: Please check that your answer is ____ before you hand in your test.
parts.explanation: You check an answer to make sure it is right, so accurate fits.

hints: The map led the scouts without any wrong turns.

subject: english
text: The aquarium wall was made of transparent glass. Visitors could see the sharks gliding past as clearly as if there were no barrier at all.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "transparent" mean?
parts.explanation: Visitors could see through it clearly, so transparent means see-through.

options.text: Clean window glass is transparent, so light passes straight through.
The transparent of the jar was high.

subject: english
text: Water is essential for every living thing. Without it, plants wilt, animals weaken and people cannot survive for long.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "essential" mean?
parts.explanation: Living things cannot survive without it, so essential means absolutely needed.

parts.prompt: A helmet is ____ when you ride a bike because it protects your head.
parts.explanation: Something that protects you and must be worn is needed, so essential fits.

hints: What happens to living things without water?

subject: english
text: The ferocious dog barked and snarled behind the fence. Its teeth flashed, and the postman wisely kept his distance.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "ferocious" mean?
parts.explanation: Barking, snarling and flashing teeth show a fierce dog, so ferocious means fierce.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "ferocious" correctly?

options.text: We ferocious the cake with chocolate.
A ferocious lion roared and chased the zebras across the plain.
We ate a ferocious slice of cake for dessert.
The ferocious of the storm kept us inside.

parts.explanation: Ferocious means fierce and wild, so a roaring lion chasing zebras fits. A purring kitten or a kind whisper is the opposite.

subject: english
text: It is necessary to wear sunscreen at the beach. Our summer sun is strong, and sunburn can happen in only twenty minutes.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "necessary" mean?
parts.explanation: Sunburn can happen quickly, so sunscreen is needed; necessary means required.

parts.prompt: Is it ____ to bring a pencil case, or will the school give us pencils?
parts.explanation: The question asks whether a pencil case is needed, so necessary fits.

hints: Why is sunscreen worn at the beach?

subject: english
text: The teacher asked us to separate the plastic bottles from the paper in the recycling bin. We put them into two different piles.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses "separate" correctly?

options.text: Please separate the red beads from the blue beads before you start.
She put the books in a separate of the shelf.

subject: english
text: Our class cleaned the creek to protect the environment. Fewer rubbish bags meant cleaner water for the fish, frogs and birds that lived there.

parts.prompt: In the passage, what does "environment" mean?
parts.explanation: Fish, frogs, birds and water make up nature around us, so environment means the natural world.

parts.prompt: Planting trees helps to protect the ____ and gives animals a home.
parts.explanation: Trees and animals are part of the natural world, so environment fits.

hints: Who benefits from cleaner water in the passage?

subject: english

options.text: Please disappear the door quietly behind you.
